extracted.intended_audience: Contracting Officers and contracting personnel implementing OMB Circular A-76 for Commercial Industrial Type Activity (CITA) procurements (DoD/Navy)
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria for conducting cost comparisons, bid openings, public review, and award decisions under OMB Circular A-76 for CITA support service procurements; focuses on Contracting Officer responsibilities, statement-of-work quality, solicitation methods, and audit/appeal handling. Includes recommended organizational, training, and regulatory changes to improve implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract price entry for CPFF contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: For Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee (CPFF) contracts, the sum of the total estimated costs and the fixed fee shall be entered on line ten of the cost comparison form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews indicated that the sum of total estimated costs and fixed fee would be entered for CPFF. No additional prescriptive guidance in Handbook beyond this practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract price entry for CPIF contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: For Cost-Plus-Incentive-Fee (CPIF) contracts, the target cost combined with the target fee shall be used as the contract price on the cost comparison form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners reported using target cost + target fee. Handbook emphasizes cost realism but does not specify line-ten entries; interviews supplied this operational convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee estimation for CPAF contracts tied to performance level
rubrics_metrics.description: For Cost-Plus-Award-Fee (CPAF) contracts, estimate the amount of the fee based on the performance level comparable to that attributed to Government employees in preparing the Government estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires the SOW to provide a standard of performance acceptable for both Government and contractor performance. OFPP working papers indicate the contract price should include estimated cost, base fee, and that portion of award fee commensurate with the Government-attributed performance level. Contracting Officer must determine appropriate portion of award fee after consultation with estimators and functional managers and by exercising informed, independent judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Time-and-Material/Labor-Hour contracts in cost comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: When Time-and-Material (T&M) or Labor-Hour contracts are used, the total estimated cost of performance may be calculated and entered, or comparable rates may be developed and the cost comparison conducted on the basis of rates rather than total costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research did not reveal instances where the rates-based method was used; Handbook indicates either approach is acceptable, but practice favors entering total estimated cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of 'contract price' for cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining the 'contract price' to be entered on the cost comparison form is a critical responsibility of the Contracting Officer and requires familiarity with methodologies for obtaining the contract price.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many contracting personnel were unaware of full responsibilities or methodologies. This determination may be among the most important responsibilities directly attributable to the Contracting Officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance of proper conduct during award cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: During the award cycle, the Contracting Officer must assure that bid opening, cost comparison, and public review are conducted in accordance with established guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officer should also monitor late in-house estimates, discrepancies in cost comparison, and considerations regarding possible protests or appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of added Government costs as award factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs to the Government that will be incurred only if a contract is awarded (e.g., transportation, contract administration, government-furnished materials, contractor use of government equipment/facilities, standby maintenance, termination costs) are award factors, not evaluation factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These 'award factors' are not used to determine offeror's grasp of requirement, expertise, to differentiate or rank offerors, to determine competitive range, are not equally applied to all offerors, and are applied only to the otherwise successful bidder/offeror. NAVMAT recommended treating them similarly to responsibility determinations and EEO compliances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealed in-house cost estimate submission timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The sealed Government in-house cost estimate must be submitted to the Contracting Officer by the required submission date for bids and proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existing directives state this, but researcher could not find written guidance on actions if the cost estimate is submitted late. Contracting personnel indicated uncertainty and varied practice (e.g., automatic extension of solicitation was suggested by some, but seen as potentially unfair).

rubrics_metrics.name: Government in-house estimate treated as a 'proposal' under late proposals clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparison clauses in negotiated solicitations include reference to 'Late Proposals, Modification of Proposals/ and Withdrawal of Proposals' and indicate the Government in-house cost estimate will be considered a proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard Form 33A provisions about late proposals generally say late proposals received after specified date will not be considered; if applied to the Government estimate it could imply rejection, creating a conflict between CITA directives and contracting clauses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison requires Government in-house estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: A cost comparison cannot be accomplished without the Government in-house cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an operational constraint: the process depends on having the in-house estimate available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer monitoring to prevent late in-house estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should closely monitor submission of the Government in-house cost estimate and take proactive steps (e.g., instruct negotiator to keep close interface with task group and extend bid opening if needed) to preclude late submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many COs had already directed negotiators to extend bid opening if it appeared the estimate might be late; this practice was seen as a pragmatic means to avoid inability to perform cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for revealing Government in-house cost estimate (formal advertising)
rubrics_metrics.description: For formally advertised procurements (including small business restricted advertising), the Government cost estimate will be revealed at bid opening; contractors and unions will be provided the in-house estimate for review at bid opening or as soon as practicable thereafter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since formal advertising satisfies cost comparison requirements, this procedure is satisfactory in those cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for revealing Government in-house cost estimate (negotiated solicitations)
rubrics_metrics.description: In negotiated solicitations the clause stipulates that at the conclusion of negotiations the Contracting Officer will set a time/place for public opening of the Government in-house estimate, provide notification, open/record the estimate, and provide copies upon request; no contractor proposal information will be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interview and researcher observations indicated this procedure was not always followed (e.g., for 8(a) set-asides). Contracting Officers felt clauses should be modified to not reveal the in-house estimate in 8(a) negotiated procurements and to restrict attendance by union representatives and some contracting personnel in such cases to preserve equity/integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding inequity when revealing in-house estimate at 8(a) proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Government in-house estimate should not be revealed in the case of 8(a) negotiated procurements because the 8(a) offeror's attendance could provide an unfair advantage for potential resolicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researcher unable to find instances where clauses were modified for 8(a). The concern: an 8(a) offeror aware of the in-house estimate could later submit lower bids in resolicitation, disadvantaging other competitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary announcement at bid opening
rubrics_metrics.description: At the bid opening the Contracting Officer must make a required public statement indicating preliminary results of the cost comparison (preliminary calculations indicate either in-house or contract operation is most economical) and note that final determination will await verification and responsibility determinations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Several personnel were not fully aware of the procedural requirement to make this statement. Failure to make it could increase misunderstandings and attacks on integrity if errors are later discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second public review and withholding award
rubrics_metrics.description: After receipt of the audited cost comparison form with approved decision summary, the Contracting Officer announces results and withholds award pending public review for a minimum of five workdays (Handbook allows five to fifteen working days).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NAVSUP questioned sufficiency of five days; if mail notification is used, five days may be consumed by mail. Experienced personnel preferred a fifteen-day review period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two verification points for discrepancies
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrepancies in the Government estimate or cost comparison process may be uncovered during (1) the independent audit of the cost comparison form and (2) the public review of the results and decision summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only minor discrepancies are noted at audit, execute the audit certificate. Significant discrepancies are reported to the Task Group Chairperson with impact and recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a 'significant discrepancy'
rubrics_metrics.description: No definitive written guidance was found; practitioners generally considered a significant discrepancy to be one that altered the relative standing between the low bidder and the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the literature lacked a definition, auditing authorities rely on professional judgment; recommendation implied need for clearer standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions when Government estimate cannot be corrected timely
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Government cost estimate cannot be corrected timely (by dates corresponding to bid/proposal expiration), appropriate actions vary: for a new start the Government estimate will be rejected and a contract awarded; for a conversion the solicitation may be cancelled, though there is no mandatory requirement to cancel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some negotiators believed cancellation necessary even under formal advertising, but they were not always familiar with different requirements for new starts versus conversions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between appeals and protests under A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB Circular A-76 directives are matters of Executive policy and not generally subject to GAO protest; the 1979 Circular specifies it does not create a procedural or substantive basis for challenge except for the internal appeals process in Section 11.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GAO has held these directives are not within its jurisdiction; appeals resolve determination between in-house and contract performance and are internal to the agency with decisions final and to be reviewed by an official at the same level or higher than the original Approving Authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Officer responsibility to determine availability of commercial sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should consider the determination of the availability of commercial sources to be one of their primary responsibilities under A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early participation by contracting personnel in the assessment phase of the CITA cycle helps achieve accurate determinations; development of sources of supply has traditionally centered on contracting expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of informational solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Informational solicitations by themselves are not satisfactory to decide retention in-house due to non-availability of commercial sources; they should be used only in conjunction with other required methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no commercial interest is expressed from informational solicitation alone, Commerce Business Daily (CBD) notices are still required before deciding to retain performance in-house based on lack of private sector interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for OFPP guidance on CBD notices
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of Federal Procurement Policy should provide more definitive guidance on the use of CBD notices, including what constitutes a sufficient response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the interim, Contracting Officers should be hesitant to use CBD notices instead of formal solicitation to avoid unnecessarily extending the acquisition process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active contracting participation in multifunctional solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should take a more active role in developing multifunctional solicitations and lead in creating single solicitation documents for the same CITA at different organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages include lower overall acquisition and contract administration costs; COs must weigh benefits against possibly favoring larger firms over small/disadvantaged businesses and coordinate early with supported organizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with communications directives to prevent premature information release
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting personnel must be totally familiar with directives on communications with interested groups (unions, Congress, industry) to prevent premature release of information that could embarrass the command or undermine system integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes careful handling of inquiries on CITA program status/progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational and staffing review for CITA workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should review organizational and staffing structures and consider establishing dedicated Service Branches or a separate Contract Administration Branch to better process CITA requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is important to prepare contracting offices to handle expanding CITA program workloads efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor implementation and resource allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Naval Supply Systems Command should monitor field activity implementation efforts and provide additional resources commensurate with program growth to avoid worsening workload situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Field contracting offices should also assure existing resources are optimally organized to support projected program expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject inadequate statements of work (SOWs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers should reject SOWs that are inadequate for solicitation purposes and require resubmission rather than attempting post-receipt corrections or updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: COs must be familiar with elements of a good CITA work statement, establish internal milestones and maintain milestone integrity through active management early in the cycle. Also recognize CITA contracting often cannot meet existing Procurement Administrative Lead Time goals; realistic standards should be provided and monitored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitize command procurement responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Naval Supply Systems Command and Naval Facilities Engineering Command should definitize agreements about which command will procure a specific service function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assists development of specialized expertise at contracting offices, and improves coordination, preparation, and submission of SOWs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish dedicated training programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices should establish dedicated training programs centered on the key reference materials identified in the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should prepare contract negotiators and contracting personnel for unique CITA concepts and for the cost comparison process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting office support for Task Group planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices should be more supportive of internal planning by the Task Group to ensure realistic milestones, accurate SOWs, and maintenance of system integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best accomplished by early coordination and schedule development with supported organizations before receipt of purchase request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise DoD and Navy directives to conform with A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: DoD and Navy directives should be revised and clarified to conform with existing A-76 policy guidelines to enhance consistent policy implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This would help field contracting offices implement policy uniformly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include separate service contracting coverage in DAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Defense Acquisition Regulation should include separate coverage of service contracting with a distinct section on CITA Support Service Contracting to eliminate confusion (clauses, 8(a) use, options, cost comparison, methodologies, late submissions, and significant discrepancy standards).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporation of the Firm Bid/Offer procedure (DAR Case 76-144) into the regulatory framework was recommended as a step toward this objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain high integrity and avoid compromising actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting professionals should take aggressive action to ensure system integrity, assess their own actions for possible compromising positions, and provide Standards of Conduct guidance to Task Group Chairpersons and members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important to maintain public faith in principles of consistency and equity expressed in the Circular.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer formal advertising and performance-oriented SOWs for conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: In most instances formal advertising methods should be used to accomplish the cost comparison for potential conversions from in-house to contractor performance, using a performance-oriented SOW that details what is to be accomplished but not how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach supports competitive fairness and focuses on outcomes rather than contractor methodology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences and site visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices should make maximum use of pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences and site visits, as many contractors are not aware of new CITA concepts and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract negotiators must be familiar with the cost comparison process to provide intelligent answers at conferences; this aids bidder understanding and competition quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide additional training for contract negotiators
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract negotiators need additional general training in the CITA program and in the cost comparison process in particular.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should include hands-on familiarity with clauses, procedures, and typical problem areas to avoid detrimental contracting actions.
